# SBOM & AI-BOM

**Goal:** produce a software bill of materials (SBOM) for your dependencies and
an AI-BOM for the models, prompts, and inference frameworks your code uses.

**Prerequisites:** Node.js ≥ 24. Both artifacts are generated by a scan, so
they work on any project — including [`examples/demo-app`](../../examples/demo-app/),
which is used for the sample output below.

---

## SBOM — your dependency inventory

An SBOM lists every third-party component with its version, license, and any
known vulnerabilities. Emit one directly from a scan:

```bash
# CycloneDX 1.6 (JSON)
npx @clear-capabilities/agentic-security-scanner scan . --format cyclonedx --output sbom.cdx.json

# SPDX 2.3 (JSON)
npx @clear-capabilities/agentic-security-scanner scan . --format spdx --output sbom.spdx.json
```

Both are standard formats consumable by any SBOM tooling. Each component
carries its `purl` (package URL), license, and — for anything with a published
advisory — the vulnerability attached inline (OSV id, CVE aliases, severity,
CVSS vector, and EPSS score where available).

### Explore it conversationally (Claude Code)

```text
/agentic-security:supply --sbom
```

This reads the last scan's SBOM and lets you ask about dependencies, version
drift, and transitive paths in plain language instead of grepping JSON.

### What's reachable, not just what's present

SCA findings are classified by reachability tier — `function-reachable`,
`import-reachable`, `build-only`, `manifest-only`, `transitive-only` — so you
fix what actually matters. Run the full supply-chain pass with:

```bash
npx @clear-capabilities/agentic-security-scanner scan . --only sca
```

or `/agentic-security:supply --check` in Claude Code, which also offers to open
a single PR bumping every *safe* (patch/minor) dependency at once.

---

## AI-BOM — your AI component inventory

If your code calls an LLM, an AI-BOM inventories the models, providers, prompt
templates, inference frameworks, and vector stores it uses — and flags what's
unpinned:

```bash
# JSON
npx @clear-capabilities/agentic-security-scanner scan . --format aibom --output aibom.json

# Markdown (readable)
npx @clear-capabilities/agentic-security-scanner scan . --format aibom-md
```

Sample output (from the demo app's `ai-assistant.js`):

```text
# AI-BOM

## Summary
| Category | Count |
|---|---|
| Models referenced | 1 |
| Distinct providers | 1 |
| Pinned (revision/SHA) | 0 |
| Unpinned | 1 |
| Inference frameworks | 1 |

## Models
| Provider | Model | Pinned | File:Line |
|---|---|---|---|
| <provider> | <model> | ❌ | ai-assistant.js:13 |
```

An unpinned model (no revision/SHA) is called out because the model behind a
floating name can change under you — the AI-supply-chain equivalent of an
unpinned dependency.

---

## Keeping it current

New CVEs land against dependencies you already have. Check now, and wire up
recurring checks:

```text
/agentic-security:supply --cve-alerts
```

This runs a one-shot check against your installed dependencies and, if you
want ongoing monitoring, helps you schedule it in CI (see [CI setup](ci-setup.md)).
